subject: Private deployment: demarc & egress handoff, telemetry and HA questions
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Perez <carlos.perez@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: demarc & egress handoff, telemetry and HA questions

Carlos / Acme networking team —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As we get closer to the on-prem cutover for the Private deployment, I want to align on a few handoff items so the control plane / data plane boundary is clear and the egress/telemetry flows meet your audit requirements. Attached is an early reference diagram (vpc-demarc-diagram_v1.pdf) and a simple interface matrix (egress-interface-matrix.xlsx).

Key asks before we lock the runbook:
- Confirm expected egress breakouts (NAT vs. proxy) and whether outbound proxy is mandatory for compliance scanning.
- Confirm whether you require direct BGP peering to our egress appliances or preferring a static SNAT model behind your egress concentrator.
- Telemetry: what retention and field-level redaction do you require for request/response traces? We propose storing token-level hashes only and redacting payloads before export.
- Control plane reachability: we'll expose a customer-dedicated control endpoint (mTLS) — which subnets and port ranges should we include in the allowlist?

Proposed next steps: 
1) Acme answers the three bullets above.
2) We iterate the diagram and produce a final runbook (cutover checklist + rollback steps).
3) Schedule a dry-run with Acme ops and Redwood infra (2 hours).

I've CC'd Irene and Kimberly from our infra team for the technical specifics and rollout readiness.

Attachments: vpc-demarc-diagram_v1.pdf, egress-interface-matrix.xlsx, telemetry-requirements.md

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Carlos Perez <carlos.perez@acme.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@acme.com>, Acme Networking Team <networks@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: demarc & egress handoff, telemetry and HA questions

Thanks Mateo — good summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Egress model: Compliance requires outbound traffic to traverse our inspection proxy for TLS termination and DLP checks. So outbound proxy is mandatory for all customer-plane egress. We can host an explicit proxy cluster in the edge rack; SNAT behind that proxy is fine.

2) Peering: We prefer not to run BGP with vendor appliances in our racks unless absolutely necessary. Please plan for static routes + SNAT at the proxy cluster. If we need dynamic reroutes later, we can discuss BGP as a later phase.

3) Telemetry: Retention — 90 days for trace metadata, 365 days aggregated metrics. Payloads containing PII must not be exported. The security team will provide a redaction spec (I'll attach). Hashes for identifiers are OK.

4) Control plane access: Allowlist will include the Redwood control plane IP block (we'll provide official CIDR). We'll allow mTLS on TCP 443 and a health-check range on 8443. No other inbound ports. Please provide expected source IP ranges for your HA pairs.

We'll review the attached diagram and matrix and send comments inline by Monday. Also: please add a note on how failover behaves when the proxy cluster is in maintenance mode.

— Carlos
Carlos Perez
Network Lead, Acme Financial Services
carlos.perez@acme.com

Attachment: acme-redaction-spec_v1.pdf
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Perez <carlos.perez@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: demarc & egress handoff, telemetry and HA questions

Carlos — thanks for the quick responses and the redaction note. Highlights from our side and adjustments to the plan: 

- Egress: we'll update the runbook to require your outbound inspection proxy as the only egress hop. Redwood egress appliances will be configured in a trunked fashion to forward through the proxy cluster; we will not advertise BGP in phase 1.

- Failover: if the proxy cluster is in maintenance, Redwood will automatically queue non-critical telemetry exports and fall back to an emergency-allowlist route to a maintenance egress IP you provide. Sensitive traffic (control plane, management) will remain blocked unless explicitly allowed by the emergency procedure. We'll document the queuing/backpressure behavior and maximum queue duration (recommended: 10 minutes) in the runbook.

- Control plane allowlist: see tentative source ranges below (these are our HA pair addresses; please confirm):
  - 10.172.200.16/32
  - 10.172.200.17/32
  - 10.172.200.18/32

Irene, can you confirm port/healthcheck behavior and the exact TLS profiles we'll require on our side? Kim — can you confirm whether the infra team can support the queuing/backpressure behavior and the 'emergency egress' route?

I'll await the official CIDRs from Acme and the redaction spec. Once we have that we can finalize the runbook and propose two dry-run windows next week.

Thanks,
Mateo
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Carlos Perez <carlos.perez@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: demarc & egress handoff, telemetry and HA questions

Quick technical clarifications: 

- Ports / Health: We'll terminate mTLS on the Redwood control endpoint (443) using the customer-provided certs. Health checks will come from an ephemeral pool on ports 8443-8445. Health checks are HTTP(s) GET /_hc returning 200. We will include HMAC headers for authenticity if you prefer.

- TLS profile: We will support TLS1.3 only for control plane connections (policy). Cipher suite: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 or stronger. If Acme needs TLS1.2 for their proxies, we can provide a compatible front-proxy but would prefer to keep controlplane TLS1.3 end-to-end.

- Telemetry export: Redwood will run an exporter that strips payloads and replaces any detected PII fields with the hash and a redaction flag. For quota reasons we propose aggregated traces once every 30s during steady-state; raw traces will be kept locally for 10 minutes before discard unless marked for retention by the customer.

- Backpressure: infra will implement an in-memory leaky-bucket queue with a 10-minute max retention window. In a sustained proxy outage we will drop non-critical metrics after that window and generate an incident.

Attachment: controlplane-tls-profile.md

Irene Choi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

All — thanks for the alignment. Operational notes and immediate asks from infra: 

1) Cutover windows: we can support two dry-run windows next Wed 2026-08-17 01:00-03:00 UTC and Thu 2026-08-18 22:00-00:00 UTC. Please confirm which works for Acme.

2) Runbook checklist (we'll author and share a living doc):
   - Validate CIDRs and update allowlists
   - Install customer certs on controlplane endpoints (mTLS)
   - Provision proxy emergency IP and test failover path
   - Run telemetry redaction test with a synthetic payload set (we'll provide the harness)
   - Execute a single-request failover test and confirm behavior

3) DocuSign / agreements: Sophie — please review and sign the network addendum we referenced. Link below.

Related attachments: final-runbook-template.docx (we will populate after CIDR confirmation)
